# Qualitygate CLI

Use this Skill to select the appropriate evidence and workflow; use the matching
`qualitygate` executable for Schema export, source binding, validation, generation,
planning and checks. An agent's interpretation never replaces a CLI result.
Preserve the user's scope, selected runtime and existing authorization.

## Choose the task before running commands

| Task | Read when applicable | Boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Verify implementation, bug fixes or refactors | [Verification](references/verification.md) | Establish the selected policy, run the final full check and retain its evidence. |
| Inspect help, capabilities or schemas; verify the runtime | [Runtime startup](references/runtime-startup.md), [compatibility](references/runtime-compatibility.md), [selfcheck](references/selfcheck.md) | These operations need no repository policy; do not initialize one for them. |
| Discover or configure rules | [Rule management](references/rule-management.md), [bundled rules](references/builtin-rules.md) | Read-only discovery can precede initialization; policy context requires the selected existing policy. Candidate edits need authorization within the current task. |
| Translate explicit repository constraints into rules | [Rule authoring](references/rule-authoring.md) | Select V1/V2/V3 by supported evidence, export the matching Schema, bind sources and validate before generation. Generation is not adoption. |
| Review responsibility, dependencies, duplicated knowledge or interface behavior | [Design review](references/design-review.md) | Apply Clean Code, Clean Architecture, DRY and SOLID to concrete contracts and counterexamples. Contextual review is not a deterministic gate. |
| Review concurrency, lifetime, bounds, cross-path behavior or tests | [Public review pack](references/review-pack.md) | Select the relevant cards and retain evidence gaps; do not infer safety from text patterns. |

Read only the references needed for the task. Runtime inspection, rule discovery
and review-only requests do not imply a full repository check or policy adoption.
For code changes, the verification workflow remains a prerequisite to completion.

## Execution and authority invariants

Use the existing repository policy and applicable task contract. Never weaken a
required check, fabricate an approval, invent a trusted ref, or suppress a missing
capability to produce a pass. Separately required repository checks still apply.
Resolve findings within the authorized task and recheck after input changes.

Code-task completion requires the final unfiltered `profile: full` report with
`scope: delivery` or `scope: task`, empty `plan.pending_delivery_checks`,
`gate.complete: true`, `gate.decision: pass` and exit code `0`, plus separately
required checks. Quick/path feedback, preflight, schema validity, prompt delivery
and warning triage each provide narrower evidence. Preserve warnings, incomplete
execution and unknowns. Follow [verification](references/verification.md) for the
complete decision and initialization procedure.

When reporting `check` or `selfcheck`, preserve `verification.conclusion`,
`verified_shapes`, `known_limits` and `unverified_assumptions`. A pass concerns
the verified shapes and scope; it is not proof of a defect-free deployment.

For rule authoring, the LLM may draft a candidate but must use the matching CLI's
source and validation results. Read the complete exported Schema and keep
unsupported obligations explicit. Do not extend the finite DSL from memory or
describe a review signal as proof of a semantic defect. Existing authorization
can cover candidate edits; approval and adoption remain separate decisions.

When effective policy declares `agent_obligations`, obtain the current
`agent-contract` projection with the selected role, task and policy before acting.
Apply its prompt to the consuming agent and reload after resume, handoff or
relevant input changes. Read [Agent contracts](references/agent-contracts.md).
Required gaps block readiness; a ready projection proves neither compliance nor
host enforcement. Preserve higher-priority instructions and existing permissions.
Required host controls need an actual supporting host, not an acknowledgement.

## Runtime and path conventions

Resolve the installed Skill and target repository independently:

| Input | Owner and path |
| --- | --- |
| `QUALITYGATE_SKILL_ROOT` | Absolute installation directory containing this `SKILL.md` |
| `QUALITYGATE_BIN` | Explicitly selected trusted executable, otherwise the matching `assets/<platform>-<architecture>/qualitygate[.exe]` or verified published PATH runtime |
| Built-in assets | Installation's `references/rules/`; optional explicit `QUALITYGATE_BUILTIN_RULES_DIR` |
| Schemas | Installation's `references/schemas/`, compared with runtime exports |
| `REPOSITORY_ROOT` | Absolute root of the target repository, when needed |
| `QUALITYGATE_CONFIG` | `qualitygate.yaml`, or the caller's normalized repository-relative `--config` path |
| Project candidates | Repository's `qualitygate/rules/`; discovery honors legacy `custom_rules` |
| Policy history | Repository's `.qualitygate/policy/` |

Use the shell-specific [startup examples](references/runtime-startup.md). Preserve
an explicit executable or asset override and report invalid selections; do not
silently replace them. Choose assets for the actual OS and architecture. Do not
build an untrusted checkout as the runtime. Version equality does not establish
build identity: inspect capabilities, executable digest and matching assets.

Carry the same `--root`, `--config` and selected policy/task inputs through relevant
commands. Reference examples without `--config` assume the default. Bind variables
again across isolated tool calls. `skill:references/rules/...` is provenance, not
a repository-relative path. Built-in YAML is runtime data; project configuration
is the candidate-edit surface. Discovery does not enable enforcement.

## Initialization prerequisite

For repository verification, follow the canonical
[configuration prerequisite](references/verification.md#initialization-prerequisite).
Confirmed missing configuration requires ordinary automatic `init`; malformed
configuration requires diagnosis. Keep discovery and runtime-only tasks outside
that prerequisite. Initialization does not authorize command adoption, rule
enabling or policy adoption.

## Additional workflows

| Need | Reference and control surface |
| --- | --- |
| Select snapshots, trim acquisition inputs or preserve trust evidence | [Operations](references/operations.md); snapshot selectors, reviewed exclusions and external evidence |
| Bound instruction size or retain required paths | [File contracts](references/file-contracts.md); `file` with `change: all` |
| Require assertion counterexamples against old code | [Test effectiveness](references/test-effectiveness.md); explicit command/task `test_effectiveness` |
| Prevent analyzer debt growth | [Diagnostic ratchets](references/diagnostic-ratchets.md); report `mode: ratchet` with a fresh base run |
| Compose typed predicates and bounded counts | [V2 operators](references/operators.md); `rules.operators.v2` |
| Relate collections with lexical lambdas and projections | [V3 operators](references/operators-v3.md); `rules.operators.v3` |
| Track declared clauses, adoption, unsupported gaps and snapshot execution | [Constraint coverage](references/constraint-coverage.md); `schema constraint`, automatic `constraint-coverage` check |
| Run the selected Rust Agent host with guarded delivery | [Agent host](references/agent-host.md); `agent-run`, injection receipts, fresh full checks and immutable export |
| Supply bounded repair context | [Agent feedback](references/agent-feedback.md); `check --feedback` and full rechecks |
| Consume versioned decisions or assess warnings | [Decision protocol](references/decision-protocol.md); schemas, optional `--envelope` and advisory judgment |
| Seal or independently accept a declared pilot inventory | [Pilot evidence](references/pilot-evidence.md); signed owner/reviewer records and full-report bindings |

File contracts and diagnostic ratchets are not additional built-in IDs for
`rules enable`. The CLI advertises actual rule definitions and parameter contracts
through `rules list` and `rules describe`; use that inventory rather than treating
this Skill's examples as exhaustive. A missing capability is a compatibility gap.
Neither a prompt's design recommendation nor an enabled pattern signal proves
that a repository satisfies Clean Architecture or SOLID.

name: qualitygate-cli
description: "Verify implementation, bug-fix and refactor changes with Qualitygate CLI, author source-bound repository rules, and review design contracts with evidence. Also use for rule configuration, runtime verification and selfcheck."

# Qualitygate CLI

Use this Skill to select the appropriate evidence and workflow; use the matching
`qualitygate` executable for Schema export, source binding, validation, generation,
planning and checks. An agent's interpretation never replaces a CLI result.
Preserve the user's scope, selected runtime and existing authorization.

## Choose the task before running commands

| Task | Read when applicable | Boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Verify implementation, bug fixes or refactors | [Verification](references/verification.md) | Establish the selected policy, run the final full check and retain its evidence. |
| Inspect help, capabilities or schemas; verify the runtime | [Runtime startup](references/runtime-startup.md), [compatibility](references/runtime-compatibility.md), [selfcheck](references/selfcheck.md) | These operations need no repository policy; do not initialize one for them. |
| Discover or configure rules | [Rule management](references/rule-management.md), [bundled rules](references/builtin-rules.md) | Read-only discovery can precede initialization; policy context requires the selected existing policy. Candidate edits need authorization within the current task. |
| Translate explicit repository constraints into rules | [Rule authoring](references/rule-authoring.md) | Select V1/V2/V3 by supported evidence, export the matching Schema, bind sources and validate before generation. Generation is not adoption. |
| Review responsibility, dependencies, duplicated knowledge or interface behavior | [Design review](references/design-review.md) | Apply Clean Code, Clean Architecture, DRY and SOLID to concrete contracts and counterexamples. Contextual review is not a deterministic gate. |
| Review concurrency, lifetime, bounds, cross-path behavior or tests | [Public review pack](references/review-pack.md) | Select the relevant cards and retain evidence gaps; do not infer safety from text patterns. |

Read only the references needed for the task. Runtime inspection, rule discovery
and review-only requests do not imply a full repository check or policy adoption.
For code changes, the verification workflow remains a prerequisite to completion.

## Execution and authority invariants

Use the existing repository policy and applicable task contract. Never weaken a
required check, fabricate an approval, invent a trusted ref, or suppress a missing
capability to produce a pass. Separately required repository checks still apply.
Resolve findings within the authorized task and recheck after input changes.

Code-task completion requires the final unfiltered `profile: full` report with
`scope: delivery` or `scope: task`, empty `plan.pending_delivery_checks`,
`gate.complete: true`, `gate.decision: pass` and exit code `0`, plus separately
required checks. Quick/path feedback, preflight, schema validity, prompt delivery
and warning triage each provide narrower evidence. Preserve warnings, incomplete
execution and unknowns. Follow [verification](references/verification.md) for the
complete decision and initialization procedure.

When reporting `check` or `selfcheck`, preserve `verification.conclusion`,
`verified_shapes`, `known_limits` and `unverified_assumptions`. A pass concerns
the verified shapes and scope; it is not proof of a defect-free deployment.

For rule authoring, the LLM may draft a candidate but must use the matching CLI's
source and validation results. Read the complete exported Schema and keep
unsupported obligations explicit. Do not extend the finite DSL from memory or
describe a review signal as proof of a semantic defect. Existing authorization
can cover candidate edits; approval and adoption remain separate decisions.

When effective policy declares `agent_obligations`, obtain the current
`agent-contract` projection with the selected role, task and policy before acting.
Apply its prompt to the consuming agent and reload after resume, handoff or
relevant input changes. Read [Agent contracts](references/agent-contracts.md).
Required gaps block readiness; a ready projection proves neither compliance nor
host enforcement. Preserve higher-priority instructions and existing permissions.
Required host controls need an actual supporting host, not an acknowledgement.

## Runtime and path conventions

Resolve the installed Skill and target repository independently:

| Input | Owner and path |
| --- | --- |
| `QUALITYGATE_SKILL_ROOT` | Absolute installation directory containing this `SKILL.md` |
| `QUALITYGATE_BIN` | Explicitly selected trusted executable, otherwise the matching `assets/<platform>-<architecture>/qualitygate[.exe]` or verified published PATH runtime |
| Built-in assets | Installation's `references/rules/`; optional explicit `QUALITYGATE_BUILTIN_RULES_DIR` |
| Schemas | Installation's `references/schemas/`, compared with runtime exports |
| `REPOSITORY_ROOT` | Absolute root of the target repository, when needed |
| `QUALITYGATE_CONFIG` | `qualitygate.yaml`, or the caller's normalized repository-relative `--config` path |
| Project candidates | Repository's `qualitygate/rules/`; discovery honors legacy `custom_rules` |
| Policy history | Repository's `.qualitygate/policy/` |

Use the shell-specific [startup examples](references/runtime-startup.md). Preserve
an explicit executable or asset override and report invalid selections; do not
silently replace them. Choose assets for the actual OS and architecture. Do not
build an untrusted checkout as the runtime. Version equality does not establish
build identity: inspect capabilities, executable digest and matching assets.

Carry the same `--root`, `--config` and selected policy/task inputs through relevant
commands. Reference examples without `--config` assume the default. Bind variables
again across isolated tool calls. `skill:references/rules/...` is provenance, not
a repository-relative path. Built-in YAML is runtime data; project configuration
is the candidate-edit surface. Discovery does not enable enforcement.

## Initialization prerequisite

For repository verification, follow the canonical
[configuration prerequisite](references/verification.md#initialization-prerequisite).
Confirmed missing configuration requires ordinary automatic `init`; malformed
configuration requires diagnosis. Keep discovery and runtime-only tasks outside
that prerequisite. Initialization does not authorize command adoption, rule
enabling or policy adoption.

## Additional workflows

| Need | Reference and control surface |
| --- | --- |
| Select snapshots, trim acquisition inputs or preserve trust evidence | [Operations](references/operations.md); snapshot selectors, reviewed exclusions and external evidence |
| Bound instruction size or retain required paths | [File contracts](references/file-contracts.md); `file` with `change: all` |
| Require assertion counterexamples against old code | [Test effectiveness](references/test-effectiveness.md); explicit command/task `test_effectiveness` |
| Prevent analyzer debt growth | [Diagnostic ratchets](references/diagnostic-ratchets.md); report `mode: ratchet` with a fresh base run |
| Compose typed predicates and bounded counts | [V2 operators](references/operators.md); `rules.operators.v2` |
| Relate collections with lexical lambdas and projections | [V3 operators](references/operators-v3.md); `rules.operators.v3` |
| Track declared clauses, adoption, unsupported gaps and snapshot execution | [Constraint coverage](references/constraint-coverage.md); `schema constraint`, automatic `constraint-coverage` check |
| Run the selected Rust Agent host with guarded delivery | [Agent host](references/agent-host.md); `agent-run`, injection receipts, fresh full checks and immutable export |
| Supply bounded repair context | [Agent feedback](references/agent-feedback.md); `check --feedback` and full rechecks |
| Consume versioned decisions or assess warnings | [Decision protocol](references/decision-protocol.md); schemas, optional `--envelope` and advisory judgment |
| Seal or independently accept a declared pilot inventory | [Pilot evidence](references/pilot-evidence.md); signed owner/reviewer records and full-report bindings |

File contracts and diagnostic ratchets are not additional built-in IDs for
`rules enable`. The CLI advertises actual rule definitions and parameter contracts
through `rules list` and `rules describe`; use that inventory rather than treating
this Skill's examples as exhaustive. A missing capability is a compatibility gap.
Neither a prompt's design recommendation nor an enabled pattern signal proves
that a repository satisfies Clean Architecture or SOLID.

# Resolve the runtime

Read only the example for the active OS and shell. Set the Skill root to the
absolute directory containing `SKILL.md`, `references/` and, in a complete
release archive, `assets/`. Runtime selection needs no repository or policy.

Preserve an explicitly selected `QUALITYGATE_BIN` (Bash) or `$QualitygateBin`
(PowerShell). It must identify the authorized absolute executable path; an
invalid explicit selection is an error, not permission to switch builds.
Otherwise prefer the matching bundled asset, then an already verified
published executable on PATH when that asset is missing or unusable. A user
may explicitly select a verified development build for authorized CLI work;
identify it as a development build rather than a published release.

Establish the selected binary's provenance before running these examples.
PATH lookup, `--version`, a capabilities response and a self-reported digest
do not authenticate a binary. Do not build a repository checkout, install a
runtime or replace an installed copy merely to make startup succeed.

Record the executable and rule-asset bindings and reapply them in each fresh
tool shell. Complete archives discover their own assets. An explicit or PATH
runtime uses this matching Skill's assets when no override was supplied.
Preserve an existing `QUALITYGATE_BUILTIN_RULES_DIR`; it names the directory
containing `core/`, `shared/` and language packages. An invalid explicit override
is an error, not a reason to select different assets. A directory's existence
does not prove its compatibility with the binary.

The examples query `--version` and capabilities only. Compare their results
using [runtime compatibility](runtime-compatibility.md). For an older runtime
without capabilities, follow that reference's history/help path; do not infer
an old version from an arbitrary command failure.

## Linux and WSL: Bash

Set `QUALITYGATE_SKILL_ROOT`. Optionally set `QUALITYGATE_BIN` to the explicitly
selected executable. Linux and WSL use Linux assets; macOS has no bundled asset
and uses an authorized explicit executable or verified PATH runtime.

```bash
: "${QUALITYGATE_SKILL_ROOT:?Set the absolute Skill directory}"
qualitygate_external_runtime=false
if [ "${QUALITYGATE_BIN+x}" = x ]; then
  test -n "$QUALITYGATE_BIN" && test -x "$QUALITYGATE_BIN" || { echo "Invalid explicit Qualitygate executable" >&2; exit 2; }
  "$QUALITYGATE_BIN" --version || exit 2
  qualitygate_external_runtime=true
else
  qualitygate_asset=""
  if [ "$(uname -s)" = Linux ]; then
    case "$(uname -m)" in
      x86_64|amd64) qualitygate_asset=linux-x86_64 ;;
      aarch64|arm64) qualitygate_asset=linux-aarch64 ;;
    esac
  fi
  QUALITYGATE_BIN="$QUALITYGATE_SKILL_ROOT/assets/$qualitygate_asset/qualitygate"
  if [ -z "$qualitygate_asset" ] || ! test -x "$QUALITYGATE_BIN" || ! "$QUALITYGATE_BIN" --version; then
    QUALITYGATE_BIN="$(command -v qualitygate)" || exit 2
    "$QUALITYGATE_BIN" --version || exit 2
    qualitygate_external_runtime=true
  fi
fi
if [ "$qualitygate_external_runtime" = true ] && [ "${QUALITYGATE_BUILTIN_RULES_DIR+x}" != x ]; then
  QUALITYGATE_BUILTIN_RULES_DIR="$QUALITYGATE_SKILL_ROOT/references/rules"
fi
if [ "${QUALITYGATE_BUILTIN_RULES_DIR+x}" = x ]; then
  test -d "$QUALITYGATE_BUILTIN_RULES_DIR" || { echo "Invalid Qualitygate rule asset directory" >&2; exit 2; }
  export QUALITYGATE_BUILTIN_RULES_DIR
fi
"$QUALITYGATE_BIN" capabilities --format json || exit 2
```

## Windows: PowerShell

Set `$QualitygateSkillRoot` to a native absolute path. Optionally set
`$QualitygateBin` to the explicitly selected executable's native absolute path.

```powershell
if (-not $QualitygateSkillRoot) { throw "Set the absolute Skill directory" }
$qualitygateExternalRuntime = $false
if ($null -ne $QualitygateBin) {
  if (-not $QualitygateBin -or -not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $QualitygateBin -PathType Leaf)) {
    throw "Invalid explicit Qualitygate executable"
  }
  & $QualitygateBin --version
  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "Explicit Qualitygate runtime is unusable" }
  $qualitygateExternalRuntime = $true
} else {
  $architecture = [System.Runtime.InteropServices.RuntimeInformation]::OSArchitecture.ToString()
  $assetDirectory = if ([System.Runtime.InteropServices.RuntimeInformation]::IsOSPlatform([System.Runtime.InteropServices.OSPlatform]::Windows)) {
    if ($architecture -eq "X64") { "windows-x86_64" }
    elseif ($architecture -eq "Arm64") { "windows-aarch64" }
  } else { $null }
  $QualitygateBin = if ($assetDirectory) {
    Join-Path $QualitygateSkillRoot "assets/$assetDirectory/qualitygate.exe"
  } else { $null }
  $qualitygateReady = $false
  if ($QualitygateBin -and (Test-Path -LiteralPath $QualitygateBin -PathType Leaf)) {
    try {
      & $QualitygateBin --version
      $qualitygateReady = $LASTEXITCODE -eq 0
    } catch { $qualitygateReady = $false }
  }
  if (-not $qualitygateReady) {
    $QualitygateBin = (Get-Command qualitygate -CommandType Application -ErrorAction Stop | Select-Object -First 1).Source
    & $QualitygateBin --version
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "Qualitygate runtime is unusable" }
    $qualitygateExternalRuntime = $true
  }
}
if ($qualitygateExternalRuntime -and -not (Test-Path Env:QUALITYGATE_BUILTIN_RULES_DIR)) {
  $env:QUALITYGATE_BUILTIN_RULES_DIR = Join-Path $QualitygateSkillRoot "references/rules"
}
if (Test-Path Env:QUALITYGATE_BUILTIN_RULES_DIR) {
  if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $env:QUALITYGATE_BUILTIN_RULES_DIR -PathType Container)) {
    throw "Invalid Qualitygate rule asset directory"
  }
}
& $QualitygateBin capabilities --format json
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "Qualitygate capabilities are unavailable" }
```

## Windows: native Git Bash/MSYS2

Native Windows `.exe` files work in Git Bash/MSYS2. Supply shell paths for the
Skill root, an explicit executable and any asset override. Linux and WSL use
the Linux example. Convert paths passed to native Windows processes explicitly.

```bash
: "${QUALITYGATE_SKILL_ROOT:?Set the absolute Skill directory}"
case "$(uname -s)" in
  MINGW*|MSYS*) ;;
  *) echo "This example requires Windows Git Bash/MSYS2" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac
qualitygate_external_runtime=false
if [ "${QUALITYGATE_BIN+x}" = x ]; then
  test -n "$QUALITYGATE_BIN" && test -x "$QUALITYGATE_BIN" || { echo "Invalid explicit Qualitygate executable" >&2; exit 2; }
  "$QUALITYGATE_BIN" --version || exit 2
  qualitygate_external_runtime=true
else
  qualitygate_asset=""
  case "$(uname -m)" in
    x86_64|amd64) qualitygate_asset=windows-x86_64 ;;
    aarch64|arm64) qualitygate_asset=windows-aarch64 ;;
  esac
  QUALITYGATE_BIN="$QUALITYGATE_SKILL_ROOT/assets/$qualitygate_asset/qualitygate.exe"
  if [ -z "$qualitygate_asset" ] || ! test -x "$QUALITYGATE_BIN" || ! "$QUALITYGATE_BIN" --version; then
    QUALITYGATE_BIN="$(command -v qualitygate)" || exit 2
    "$QUALITYGATE_BIN" --version || exit 2
    qualitygate_external_runtime=true
  fi
fi
if [ "$qualitygate_external_runtime" = true ] && [ "${QUALITYGATE_BUILTIN_RULES_DIR+x}" != x ]; then
  QUALITYGATE_BUILTIN_RULES_DIR="$QUALITYGATE_SKILL_ROOT/references/rules"
fi
if [ "${QUALITYGATE_BUILTIN_RULES_DIR+x}" = x ]; then
  test -d "$QUALITYGATE_BUILTIN_RULES_DIR" || { echo "Invalid Qualitygate rule asset directory" >&2; exit 2; }
  QUALITYGATE_BUILTIN_RULES_DIR="$(cygpath -m "$QUALITYGATE_BUILTIN_RULES_DIR")" || exit 2
  export QUALITYGATE_BUILTIN_RULES_DIR
fi
MSYS2_ENV_CONV_EXCL=QUALITYGATE_BUILTIN_RULES_DIR MSYS2_ARG_CONV_EXCL='*' \
  "$QUALITYGATE_BIN" capabilities --format json || exit 2
```

Use the same per-command conversion exclusions for later native invocations.
For repository commands convert the root with `cygpath -m`; keep `--config`
repository-relative. The [verification workflow](verification.md#inspect-configuration)
provides configuration-inspection examples for each shell.

## Continue with the requested mode

For installation or evaluator regression, use [selfcheck](selfcheck.md).
Help, capabilities and schema export also require no repository initialization.
Read-only rule discovery may inspect a repository without creating policy;
follow [rule management](rule-management.md).

For a repository check, follow [verification](verification.md) to establish the
selected policy and inspect preflight evidence. Runtime resolution alone does
not require `config --show`, `init`, doctor or a formal check.

# Runtime compatibility and doctor evidence

Use [runtime startup](runtime-startup.md) to select the executable. Compare
`--version` with Skill metadata, inspect
`--help`, then query `capabilities --format json` when advertised. Validate with
[capabilities schema](schemas/capabilities.schema.json). Record the executable
SHA-256, not just the version: builds with equal versions may differ. If the
capability command is absent, use the history table and `check --help`; do not
invent a capabilities response or relabel an arbitrary parse error as age.
Identity and compatibility evidence do not authenticate the binary's provenance.
Require capabilities for the requested operation; reading this reference does
not turn a runtime query or selfcheck into repository verification.

| Capability | First published version | Verified history |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Declared bounded tool version probes | v0.3.0 | `a7f9550` belongs to v0.3.0 |
| File contracts and report ratchets | v0.4.0 | `baa1eb3` belongs to v0.4.0 |
| `exclude`, `--snapshot-max-file-mib`, `init.snapshot_preflight` | v0.5.5 | `98c0a66`; absent in v0.5.1–v0.5.4 tagged source |
| Capabilities, runtime requirements, environment requirements and doctor | v0.5.7 | `82f51a8`; require exported capability IDs; v0.5.6 lacks these additions |
| Constraint coverage and typed bounded operators | v0.5.8 | `aaa82ff`, `59c91f5`; require `constraints.coverage.v1` and `rules.operators.v2` |
| Consuming-agent contracts, Rust host and immutable delivery | v0.5.8 | `a780603`, `4579f40`, `8c4488a`; require `agent.contracts.v1`, `agent.host.v1` and `agent.delivery.v1` |
| Default document/media exclusions, retention and classified inventory evidence | v0.5.9 | `be889e9`; require `snapshot.unstructured-documents.v1` |
| Named collections and lexical lambdas | v1.0.0 | `b8cb5c8`; require `rules.operators.v3` and export `schema operator-rule-v3`; v1/v2 remain supported. |

From v0.5.9, default document/media exclusions also apply to existing policies.
Compare `snapshot.unstructured-documents.v1` when relying on this behavior.
Restore command dependencies with `unstructured_documents.retain`, or set
`enabled: false` to disable defaults. See [operations](operations.md#default-document-and-media-acquisition-exclusions).

Repository preflight uses v0.5.7 or a later compatible runtime. Require
`runtime.capabilities.v1` and `doctor.static.v1`; require `config.requires.v1`,
`command.required-env.v1` and `doctor.tool-probes.v1` when using those contracts.
Old runtime conclusions remain valid only for the inspected build. Select an
already verified compatible install or report the capability gap. Existing
authorization may cover selecting or updating a development build; use the
[implementation workflow](selfcheck.md) for its verification. Do not delete
unsupported fields or lower requirements to accommodate an incompatible binary.

The [verification workflow](verification.md) owns configuration prerequisites,
doctor invocation and final-check acceptance. Preserve its selected root/config,
snapshot, profile, task, policy and acquisition budgets. Doctor currently has no
MR selector; retain that preflight gap without changing the requested comparison.

Default doctor only inspects prerequisites. `--probe-tools` executes selected
`tools[].argv` in private snapshots, in sequence, with a shared 120-second budget
and each probe's timeout. It never executes `checks[].argv`. Select probes when
the task authorizes producer execution; a normal requested repository check
already includes these declared probes. Do not claim installation/dependency
readiness from executable presence alone. Doctor does not infer environment
names embedded in scripts; declare `required_env` in command checks or task
verification. Names must exist and have nonempty values; never print values.
Formal check enforces the declarations too.

For a runtime advertising `doctor.summary.v1`, `--summary --format json` avoids
terminal truncation. Apply it to the requested doctor invocation.

Default table/Markdown output also uses this summary. The
[summary schema](schemas/doctor-summary.schema.json) is separate from the full
doctor schema. `report.path` names a retained `qualitygate-doctor-*/report.json`
in OS temporary storage; `report.digest` and `report.bytes` identify its contents.
Read the saved report to inspect all diagnostics, identities, budgets, unexecuted
items and `next_steps[].command`. Summary details are limited to five diagnostics
and five next steps, with 240 characters of each text field; counts are complete
and `details_truncated` signals omitted summary detail. The saved report retains
the existing full protocol, including its own inventory detail limits.
Exit 2 still means blocked/incomplete. A failed write or the 16 MiB report limit
returns `report.write_failed` and `report: null`, never a successful receipt.
Delete the private temporary directory when finished; it survives CLI exit and
is not governed by `QUALITYGATE_HOME`. No repository output files are created.
Older runtimes retain `--format json`; redirect stdout to a temporary file and
capture the CLI exit status before parsing it. Do not pass an unsupported flag.

Validate the report with [doctor schema](schemas/doctor.schema.json). Retain
`scope: preflight`, identities, requested probe scope, diagnostics, unexecuted
items, pending checks and `next_steps`. Treat `next_steps[].command` as argv and
check it against the requested scope and existing authorization before execution.
Exit 0 means the requested preflight passed, not delivery acceptance. Exit 2 is
blocked/incomplete. Doctor's temporary probe evidence is not a check credential.
For a repository verification task, return to the verification workflow for the
formal check. A doctor-only request ends with its preflight evidence and limits.

`runtime.version_too_old` and `runtime.capability_missing` require a compatible
build; `config.unknown_field`, `config.type` and `config.syntax` require inspection
of the original error and available field/line/column. These are distinct from
an absent selected policy; use the verification workflow to handle that case.

## Acquisition diagnostics

Inspect selected-snapshot budgets. `init.snapshot_preflight` is the advisory
HEAD/worktree discovery report; doctor distinguishes base/index/diff inventories,
full counts, total bytes, unsupported entries and protected exclusions.

Default capacity remains 2 MiB; the maximum is 8 MiB. Prefer the smallest
sufficient integer MiB suggestion. Raising total `--snapshot-max-mib` does not
raise the per-file limit. Use metadata or repository instructions to justify a
capacity change. Above 8 MiB, review explicit policy exclusions for
unrelated resources; never automatically exclude or alter verification inputs.
Excluded files are unavailable to commands. Base-only oversize still matters,
and truncated detail lists retain complete counts. Follow
[snapshot and policy selection](operations.md#snapshot-and-policy-selection)
and [repository verification](verification.md) when applying a reviewed change.

# Progressive discovery and candidate configuration

Built-in discovery works without a repository configuration and does not change
rule selection. Use the selected `--root` and `--config` consistently:

```bash
qualitygate rules categories --format json
qualitygate rules list --category test --language rust --source builtin --format json
qualitygate rules describe test-naming --format json
```

Reading a frozen policy context also requires a Git reference containing the
selected configuration; an absent configuration at `HEAD` is an error:

```bash
qualitygate rules context --category test --policy-ref <selected-ref> --format json
```

[Repository verification](verification.md) owns the missing-configuration and
initialization workflow. Discovery does not bypass that prerequisite for checks.

For a candidate-policy change covered by the task's existing authorization, use
validated CLI mutations:

```bash
qualitygate rules categories create migration --description "API migration" --format json
qualitygate rules assign import-boundary --category migration --format json
qualitygate rules categories rename migration api-migration --format json
qualitygate rules configure import-boundary --param 'forbidden_imports.rust=["^crate::interfaces"]' --format json
qualitygate rules enable import-boundary --format json
qualitygate rules disable import-boundary --format json
qualitygate rules categories delete api-migration --force --format json
```

Use only the caller's actual import boundary. Categories are mutable labels;
assignment does not activate a rule. Starter names are core, test, security,
architecture, style and project. Rename preserves starter identity and moves
assignments atomically. Delete needs `--force` when explicit assignments remain;
forced removal removes only that category's memberships. Repeated assignments
add categories, and `rules unassign <id> --category <name>` removes one. Removing
the last explicit membership restores the origin default; if that origin was
deleted, the rule has no category until reassigned. Rule rows expose the full
`categories` array and a legacy first `category`.

Filtered reads always retain `mandatory` rules and `mandatory_checks` separately
from selected rows. Context uses this policy precedence:

- An active signed policy selects the immutable active package, including when
  `--policy-ref` is omitted. A supplied ref must match the active reference;
  historical replay belongs to candidate validation.
- Without an active policy, `--policy-ref <selected-ref>` reads the configuration
  and rules from that commit and reports `caller_supplied_ref` trust.
- Without either, context reads the local candidate with `local_candidate` trust.

Read the returned `policy_digest` and trust label. A caller-selected ref alone
is not independent approval. `rules categories list` is also accepted.

`rules describe` exposes parameter types, descriptions, defaults and schema
fragments; language descriptors also expose whether the effective parameter is
required. A fixed scope requires the declared list; a subset scope accepts only
a nonempty subset of declared languages. Omit an override to inherit its default,
rather than using an empty list to bypass scope. Schema string-length checks do
not replace UTF-8 byte budgets, Rust regex validation or other semantic checks.
`--param key=JSON` requires JSON values, including quoted strings. Dotted paths
retain sibling object values; an undotted object replaces the entire parameter.
Repeat `--param` for one atomic edit. `configure` also accepts `--severity` and
`--required true|false`; new configured rules start disabled. Project DSL
assertions are managed in rule definitions, not through parameters. Built-in
`diagnostic` message/fix metadata belongs to the shipped rule definition and
changes presentation only; it is not a configurable policy parameter or verdict.

All mutations require an existing candidate config and support `--config`.
They preserve unrelated settings and inherited defaults, validate before atomic
replacement, preserve file permissions and reject conflicting writers. A killed
writer leaves `<config>.lock`; verify that it has stopped before explicitly
recovering the lock. Retain mutation JSON (operation, changed flag, before/after
digests and result) with the command log and reviewed Git diff. Changed YAML is
normalized; semantic no-ops preserve original bytes.

Source reviews and policy trust remain separate. Executable changes can make
existing source-review bindings stale; check reports retain missing/stale
evidence. Neither a category operation nor configuration success approves a
policy or establishes a passing gate.

Discovery reads policy/rule directories without scanning repository sources.
Once an evidence/policy archive exists, semantic policy edits require an explicit
candidate ID. Use `policy candidate create` with the caller-selected parent,
actor, reason and retained evidence, followed by `policy candidate rules`.
After signed promotion, `rules context`, inventory and ordinary checks select
the immutable active package; category edits cannot weaken mandatory rules.

For an authorized policy evolution workflow, use externally supplied suite,
trust and approval files. External protected files and retained logs accept
native absolute paths on Windows and POSIX; they must remain outside the
checked repository, without traversal or symlink ancestors, within read limits.
Repository-relative rule paths still require forward slashes.
See [operations](operations.md) for snapshot materialization, external temporary
storage and execution budgets. Missing or changed inputs remain incomplete;
reducing the checked inventory is not a repair.
`policy candidate validate` compares pinned replay,
held-out and anchor tasks with bounded parallelism. `policy candidate
approval-subject` produces the exact signing subject, `approve` verifies the
independent human signature, and `promote` rechecks it before activation.
Never manufacture an approval or private key. Missing tools/evidence and
timeouts remain incomplete. `policy rollback-subject` and `policy rollback`
require a distinct external signature and preserve the historical transition.

`rules revalidate`, `demote`, `deprecate`, `retire` and `revoke` take
`--candidate`, `--actor` and `--reason`; they prepare candidate changes and do
not grant approval. `rules history` exposes evidence and lifecycle states.
`policy effectiveness` separates oracle validity, observed rule/check use and
runtime from unknown downstream benefit, context tokens and review effort.
Only results with matching suite, parent, evaluator epoch/digest, environment,
budget and job count share a longitudinal group.
Project rule reads and schema parsing use at most eight workers, with 256 files,
1 MiB content and 4,096 directory-entry limits. Catalog errors and timeouts remain
errors even when the selected category would otherwise be empty.

# Bundled built-in rule guide

The YAML files in `references/rules/` are the versioned built-in rule assets read by the
matching Qualitygate CLI at runtime. Read this guide and the relevant YAML
before proposing a rule. Then use `qualitygate rules list --format json` to
verify what the installed executable can enforce. Do not edit the Skill assets
to change a repository policy; a repository policy selects and configures
rules, while the executable owns evaluation.

## Selection boundary

Use `rules list --language java --source builtin --format json` for built-ins,
`--source project` for `qualitygate/rules` (or an explicit legacy policy path),
and `--source all` for both. An empty definition language scope adds no language
filter; each implementation still determines supported files and capabilities.
Built-in inventory queries need no initialized policy and include all shipped
packages, even unselected ones; listing does not enable enforcement. When IDs
overlap, both origins remain visible and only the selected one can be enabled.

Listing a rule is read-only. Adding or enabling rules changes candidate policy
and must be covered by the task's authorization; do not ask again when it is
already provided. Ordinary initialization follows the automatic missing-config
prerequisite in [repository verification](verification.md); it does not authorize
`--with-checks`, rule enabling, or policy adoption. A rule's archived
`standard_refs` and `lifecycle_inputs` are provenance for the packaged
definition, not an implicit mandate for every repository.

Prefer the smallest rule set that matches the user's request. A warning can
produce diagnostics while leaving the overall gate non-blocking; it still
needs a reported disposition. Missing syntax, policy, snapshot, or required
execution evidence is incomplete validation, never a clean result.

## General language rules

| Rule | Languages | Default | Use it for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `test-naming` | Java, Python, Rust, TypeScript, Go | error | added test discovery names |
| `test-naming-strict` | Java | error | added test names matching a team pattern |
| `test-annotation-dependency` | Java | error | annotated added tests and resolved Maven dependency facts |
| `no-hardcoded-secrets` | Java | error | literal credential patterns in added files |
| `no-printf-log` | C, C++ | error | `printf` or `fprintf` call patterns in added native files |
| `no-unsafe-string` | C, C++ | error | `strcpy`, `sprintf`, `strcat`, or `gets` call patterns in added native files |
| `no-test-sleep` | all languages | error | `sleep`, `usleep`, or `nanosleep` call patterns in added test paths |
| `no-bare-except` | Python | error | bare exception handler patterns in added files |
| `no-os-path` | Python | error | selected `os.path` calls in added files |
| `no-print` | Python | warning | `print` calls in added files |
| `no-emoji` | all languages | error | configured emoji Unicode ranges in added UTF-8 files |
| `python-test-naming` | Python | error | lower snake case added pytest test names |
| `parameterized-tests` | Java, Python, Rust, TypeScript, Go | warning | repeated added test shapes |
| `comment-language` | supported parsed comments | warning | an explicitly selected comment-language convention |
| `security-sensitive-api` | Java, Python, Rust, TypeScript, Go | warning | changed uses of configured high-risk API patterns |
| `todo-marker` | supported source files | warning | changed `TODO`, `FIXME`, or `XXX` work markers |

`security-sensitive-api` uses bounded, single-line regex patterns on changed
source lines: Java process launch APIs, Python `eval`/`exec` and pickle loads,
Rust `unsafe` blocks, TypeScript dynamic evaluation/process execution, and Go
process execution. A match is a review signal, not proof of an exploitable
path. Override `parameters.prohibited_patterns` only with reviewed,
language-keyed regex arrays. `paths` can narrow files; `languages` must remain a
nonempty subset of the declared languages. An omitted override inherits the
scope; `languages: []` is rejected. Consult `rules describe security-sensitive-api`
for the runtime parameter contract before editing.

`todo-marker` uses the same bounded changed-line engine. It asks for an
explicit decision about deferred work rather than assuming that every marker is
a defect or should be deleted.

`commit-message-convention` is a core rule with a ticket-prefixed default
subject pattern. Configure `parameters.pattern` for the team's convention.
`test-naming-strict` defaults to `^should_.+_when_.+` on added Java tests.
`test-annotation-dependency` defaults to `@Test` and
`org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter-api`; set `annotation`, `group`, and
`artifact` to the actual project contract, and provide a snapshot-bound Maven
facts producer through `depends_on`. Missing facts are incomplete validation
when an annotated added test is selected; an empty selection passes without a
configured producer prerequisite. Configured prerequisites still run.
`no-hardcoded-secrets` checks added Java files with a configurable single-line
regex and does not prove that every secret or live credential was found.
These Java rules are opt-in and keep a fixed Java scope.

The three Issue 10 rules are also opt-in. `no-printf-log` and
`no-unsafe-string` inspect added C/C++ files with a fixed `languages: [c, cpp]`
scope, including `.h` headers. `no-test-sleep` uses an empty language scope
and defaults to common test directory and filename globs; configure `paths`
for a repository's test layout. All three scan UTF-8 file lines with bounded
regular expressions. Matches in comments and strings can be false positives;
they do not establish a parsed call or prove that a replacement API is safe.
Files outside the selected paths, modified files, and nonmatching languages
are not inspected. Unreadable selected bytes or exhausted analysis budgets
make the check incomplete.

The six Issue 11 rules are opt-in: the four added-file rules above, the
`python-test-naming` syntax rule, and core `commit-message-format`.
The latter checks added commit subjects against a configurable subset of
Conventional Commits. `python-test-naming` sees `test`-prefixed Python
functions, including names like `test1`, then applies
the stricter default `test_` lower snake case pattern. Configure `paths` to
select pytest test files; syntax parsing alone cannot prove file collection.
`no-print` defaults
to warning; its finding does not block an otherwise complete gate.
The file rules scan UTF-8 text line by line and can match comments or
strings. `no-emoji` covers only the configured ranges in files, not commit
messages or every emoji sequence. PEP 8 allows narrow bare exception
handlers, and PEP 428 does not require every project to replace `os.path`.

## TypeScript and JavaScript review signals

Select `rulesets: [lang-typescript]` and the desired rule IDs. All fifteen
rules are opt-in and fixed to `languages: [typescript]`, which includes
`.ts`, `.tsx`, `.js`, `.jsx`, `.mjs` and `.cjs`. The original twelve inspect changed UTF-8
lines with bounded `source-pattern` matching and accept `paths` and
`prohibited_patterns.typescript` overrides. A pattern can match a comment or
string and cannot establish data flow, receiver type or production reachability.
The two comment rules cover only same-line syntax; the contact marker rule
does not classify personal data. Use the [ESLint reference](eslint-ratchet.yaml)
for semantic lint results.

| Rule | Default | Review signal |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ts-no-eval` | error | direct eval call |
| `ts-no-debugger` | error | standalone debugger statement |
| `ts-no-alert` | warning | browser dialog call |
| `ts-no-implied-eval` | error | string passed to timer callback |
| `ts-no-new-function` | error | dynamic Function constructor |
| `ts-eqeqeq` | warning | loose equality operator |
| `ts-no-extend-native` | error | direct native prototype assignment |
| `ts-no-prototype-builtins` | warning | direct prototype method call |
| `ts-secure-randomness` | warning | Math.random call for review |
| `ts-no-unsafe-postmessage` | warning | postMessage call for origin review |
| `ts-no-commented-code` | warning | code-like line comment |
| `ts-no-personal-info-in-comments` | warning | contact marker in same-line comment |
| `ts-no-with` | warning | with statement |
| `ts-no-var` | warning | var declaration |
| `ts-no-arguments` | warning | arguments object reference |

## Go review signals

Select `rulesets: [lang-go]` and the desired rule IDs. All fifteen rules are
opt-in and fixed to `languages: [go]`. The original twelve inspect changed UTF-8 `.go` lines with
bounded `source-pattern` matching. Those rules accept `paths` and
`prohibited_patterns.go` overrides. Comments and strings can match. SQL
formatting does not establish taint, `math/rand` may serve nonsecurity uses,
the panic rule does not determine function visibility, and the cgo rule does
not prove a missing free. Use the [golangci-lint reference](golangci-lint-ratchet.yaml)
for semantic lint results.

| Rule | Default | Review signal |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `go-sql-injection` | error | SQL keyword in same-line fmt.Sprintf or string concatenation |
| `go-insecure-randomness` | warning | math/rand import or common call |
| `go-tls-insecure-skip-verify` | error | literal InsecureSkipVerify true |
| `go-hardcoded-credentials` | error | literal credential assignment |
| `go-ssh-insecure-ignore-host-key` | error | InsecureIgnoreHostKey call |
| `go-file-permission-creation` | warning | literal 0666 or 0777 mode in file write call |
| `go-panic-in-exported-function` | warning | panic call for visibility review |
| `go-cgo-cstring-without-defer-free` | warning | C.CString or C.CBytes allocation call |
| `go-relative-import-path` | warning | relative import path |
| `go-dot-import` | warning | dot import outside reviewed exceptions |
| `go-sensitive-info-in-log` | warning | sensitive variable name in log call |
| `go-float-loop-counter` | warning | floating literal for-loop initializer |
| `go-unsafe-package` | warning | unsafe package usage |
| `go-os-exit` | warning | os.Exit or runtime.Goexit call |
| `go-import-alias` | warning | aliased import |

## C and C++ review signals

Select `rulesets: [lang-c]` and individual rule IDs. The seven original rules
use changed-line `source-pattern` matching with `paths` and
`prohibited_patterns.c` / `.cpp` overrides. These regex signals may match
comments or strings. The three new rules (`c-no-atoi`, `c-no-goto`,
`c-no-process-launch`) instead use bounded `native-syntax` parsing and accept
only `paths` and their fixed `languages: [c, cpp]` scope. `.c` uses the C grammar; `.h`, `.cc`, `.cpp`, `.cxx`, `.hh`, `.hpp`, `.hxx`
use the C++ grammar (which also recognizes C header syntax). This avoids
rejecting C++ declarations in ambiguously named `.h` files.
They ignore comments and literals, and inspect syntax intersecting changed
lines. Direct API calls accept unqualified, global and `std::` names, but
exclude member calls and other namespaces. Unqualified shadowing cannot be
resolved. None of these rules establishes type safety, data flow or CERT
compliance. Use the [GCC SARIF ratchet reference](gcc-analyzer-ratchet.yaml)
for semantic analyzer evidence.
The internal clauses come from the C V5.3 and C++ V5.1 language specifications;
the older C&C++ secure coding V3.0 document is explicitly superseded
and is not the current source.

| Rule | Default | Review signal |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `c-array-safety` | error | variable-bound array declaration |
| `c-assertion-discipline` | warning | increment or decrement inside `assert` |
| `c-control-flow` | warning | empty `for` condition or floating loop declaration |
| `c-expression-safety` | warning | increment or decrement inside `sizeof` |
| `c-file-security` | error | `mktemp` or `tmpnam` call |
| `c-function-safety` | warning | `abort`, `exit`, `realloc`, `alloca`, `pthread_exit` or `ExitThread` call |
| `c-numeric-literal` | error | lowercase `l` integer suffix |
| `c-no-atoi` | warning | `atoi`, `atol`, `atoll` or `atof` call |
| `c-no-goto` | warning | `goto` statement |
| `c-no-process-launch` | warning | `system`, `popen`, `exec*`, `WinExec`, `CreateProcess` or `ShellExecute` call |

## C++ review signals

Select `rulesets: [lang-cpp]` and individual rule IDs. These rules
are opt-in with fixed `languages: [cpp]`; `cpp-disabled-test` is described under
[historical review signals](#historical-review-signals). The original nine use
same-line `source-pattern` checks and accept `paths` / `prohibited_patterns.cpp`.
The seven new rules from `cpp-no-reinterpret-cast` through
`cpp-no-using-namespace-in-header` use `native-syntax`, accept only `paths`
and the fixed language scope, and also parse `.h` as C++.

Syntax rules skip comments, ordinary/raw strings and character literals.
They handle multiline syntax and report nodes intersecting diff-added lines;
unchanged syntax is not reported. The header rule covers changed `.h`, `.hh`,
`.hpp`, `.hxx` files, including existing headers. Smart-pointer checks recognize
explicit `std::unique_ptr` / `std::shared_ptr` construction with a direct `new`
argument, using parentheses or braces. Numeric macros require an object-like
macro whose replacement is a single numeric literal (optionally signed or
parenthesized), including trailing comments; expression/function macros are
outside that rule's scope.

Parsing is limited to 4 MiB, 200,000 syntax nodes and two seconds per file,
within the shared 30-second rule budget and diagnostic output budget.
Invalid UTF-8, syntax errors, missing snapshot files or exhausted budgets
produce incomplete execution, never a successful empty result. Macro expansion,
conditional-compilation evaluation, typedefs, namespace aliases, shadowing and
symbol/type resolution are not performed; syntax in conditional branches can
be reported regardless of build configuration. Warning findings require review,
not automatic replacement. Use the [Clang SARIF reference](clang-static-analyzer-ratchet.yaml)
or [GCC reference](gcc-analyzer-ratchet.yaml) for semantic analyzer evidence.

| Rule | Default | Review signal |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cpp-no-realloc` | warning | direct `realloc` call |
| `cpp-no-alloca` | warning | direct `alloca` call |
| `cpp-no-unsafe-memfunc` | error | unbounded C string call |
| `cpp-throw-by-value` | warning | `throw new` expression |
| `cpp-catch-by-reference` | warning | simple class-like value catch |
| `cpp-no-direct-mutex` | warning | direct `.lock()` or `.unlock()` call |
| `cpp-no-std-move-local-return` | warning | `return std::move(...)` expression |
| `cpp-no-unsafe-rand` | warning | `rand()` call |
| `cpp-no-throw-spec` | warning | simple empty `throw()` specification |
| `cpp-no-reinterpret-cast` | warning | `reinterpret_cast` expression |
| `cpp-no-const-cast` | warning | `const_cast` expression |
| `cpp-no-delete-this` | warning | `delete this` expression |
| `cpp-prefer-make-smart-pointer` | warning | `unique_ptr` or `shared_ptr` constructed from `new` |
| `cpp-use-nullptr` | warning | `NULL` token in C++ code |
| `cpp-no-macro-constant` | warning | numeric `#define` constant |
| `cpp-no-using-namespace-in-header` | warning | `using namespace` in a changed header |

## Python review signals

Select `rulesets: [lang-python]` and the desired rule IDs. All sixteen rules
are opt-in and fixed to `languages: [python]`. The original thirteen inspect changed UTF-8 `.py`
lines with bounded `source-pattern` matching. Those rules accept `paths` and
`prohibited_patterns.python` overrides. Calls and names are review signals:
they do not prove tainted input, credential validity, production use, safe YAML
Loader selection or sensitive log content. Use the [Ruff reference](ruff-ratchet.yaml)
for semantic lint results.

| Rule | Default | Review signal |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `py-eval-exec` | error | direct eval or exec call |
| `py-shell-equals-true` | error | same-line subprocess call with shell=True |
| `py-insecure-randomness` | warning | common random module call |
| `py-tls-verify-disabled` | error | literal verify=False assignment |
| `py-yaml-unsafe-load` | error | yaml.load call for Loader review |
| `py-sql-string-format` | error | same-line formatted execute argument |
| `py-hardcoded-credentials` | error | credential-like name assigned a literal |
| `py-tempfile-mktemp` | error | tempfile.mktemp call |
| `py-bare-except` | warning | bare except clause |
| `py-mutable-default-argument` | warning | list, dict or set default in same-line function |
| `py-assert-in-production` | warning | assert statement for context review |
| `py-sensitive-info-in-log` | warning | credential-like name in logging call |
| `py-pickle-load` | error | pickle, shelve or marshal load call |
| `py-none-comparison` | warning | equality comparison against None |
| `py-walrus-operator` | warning | assignment expression |
| `py-lambda-assignment` | warning | lambda assigned to a name |

## Structured language reviews

The twelve rules `py-none-comparison`, `py-walrus-operator`,
`py-lambda-assignment`, `go-unsafe-package`, `go-os-exit`, `go-import-alias`,
`ts-no-with`, `ts-no-var`, `ts-no-arguments`, `shell-eval`, `shell-alias` and
`shell-chmod-read` use `language-syntax`. They accept `paths` and their fixed
`languages` only; regex overrides are rejected. Tree-sitter parses immutable
selected source, including multiline syntax. Comments and literal text do not
trigger findings, while expressions inside interpolated strings and command
substitutions are inspected. Findings require changed syntax tokens.

Python checks adjacent equality operands against `None`, assignment expressions,
and named lambda assignments. Go resolves actual standard-library import paths,
including grouped, named and dot imports, with file-local lexical shadowing.
Changed imports also review retained calls; changed unsafe imports are reported
once. Named import aliases exclude blank and dot imports. TypeScript checks
`with`, `var` and implicit function `arguments`, including inherited arrow use;
properties, explicit bindings and type-only parameters are excluded.
Shell checks actual commands with static quoted names and `command`/`builtin`
wrappers. Alias queries are excluded. `chmod` examines its symbolic mode operand
for removal of read permission from all classes, not filenames or final effective
permissions; recursion is not required. Dynamic command names/modes, runtime
aliases, cross-file type resolution and ambiguous Go keyed-field names are outside
this analysis. Findings remain optional review warnings, not safety proofs.

Parsing is bounded to 4 MiB per file, 200,000 traversal/binding work steps and a
2-second per-file deadline, within shared rule time and diagnostic budgets.
Invalid UTF-8, malformed syntax and exhausted budgets produce incomplete execution.

## Rust review signals

All three Rust rules are opt-in source patterns with fixed `languages: [rust]`.
They inspect changed UTF-8 lines and allow `paths` and
`prohibited_patterns.rust` overrides. They do not establish FFI safety,
attacker-controlled paths or macro expansion safety. The macro rule covers
same-line definitions only; comments and strings may match. Use the
[Clippy ratchet reference](clippy-ratchet.yaml) for semantic lint analysis.

| Rule | Default | Review signal |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `rust-extern-without-abi` | warning | extern block opening without an ABI string |
| `rust-untrusted-dynamic-library-loading` | error | nonliteral dynamic library path argument |
| `rust-unsafe-block-in-macro-definition` | warning | unsafe block in a same-line macro definition |

## Shell conventions

All twenty-one Shell rules are opt-in and use a fixed `shell` scope. Source
patterns inspect changed lines in `.sh`, `.bash`, and extensionless scripts
with a recognized `sh` or `bash` shebang. Each accepts `paths`; the sixteen
source-pattern rules accept `prohibited_patterns.shell` overrides. They are
lexical review signals, not proof of an exploit or broken execution. Comments,
strings, valid uses of `exec`, checksums, signal numbers, and continued pipelines
can match. The password-read pattern covers simple forms, not every flag
combination. The stream-merge pattern targets a following conflicting
redirection. `shell-missing-shebang` checks added scripts and changed first
lines; a file with no extension or shebang cannot be identified as Shell.
`shell-commented-dead-code` requires three consecutive code-like comments
with at least one added line. Selected invalid UTF-8 and exceeded budgets
remain incomplete.

| Rule | Default | Review signal |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `shell-hardcoded-secret` | error | Flag quoted credential assignments |
| `shell-debug-mode` | warning | Review xtrace and verbose shell execution |
| `shell-env-dump` | warning | Review environment dump commands |
| `shell-weak-crypto` | warning | Review legacy algorithm tokens in shell scripts |
| `shell-password-echo` | warning | Review password reads without silent mode |
| `shell-sql-injection` | error | Flag database client commands with interpolated variables |
| `shell-exec-terminates` | warning | Review exec replacing the current shell |
| `shell-assignment-spaces` | error | Flag spaces adjacent to Shell assignment operators |
| `shell-comparison-spaces` | error | Flag comparison delimiters missing inner spaces |
| `shell-line-start-operator` | warning | Review leading pipe or logical operators |
| `shell-stream-merge-position` | warning | Review stream merges followed by conflicting redirections |
| `shell-trap-uncapturable` | error | Flag traps for SIGKILL or SIGSTOP |
| `shell-trap-numeric-signal` | warning | Review numeric trap signal identifiers |
| `shell-trap-double-quotes` | warning | Review double-quoted trap handlers |
| `shell-tilde-path` | warning | Review tilde path components |
| `shell-temp-file-hardcoded` | warning | Review predictable temporary paths |
| `shell-missing-shebang` | error | first-line interpreter directive on added Shell scripts |
| `shell-commented-dead-code` | warning | three or more consecutive code-like comment lines |
| `shell-eval` | warning | eval usage in a script |
| `shell-alias` | warning | alias definition in a script |
| `shell-chmod-read` | warning | chmod removing read permission |

## Architecture rules

`import-boundary` is packaged for Java, Python, Rust, TypeScript, and Go, but
is disabled by default. It checks only added syntax imports and deliberately
requires an explicit `forbidden_imports` mapping when enabled. It cannot prove
resolved dependency direction, runtime reachability, or a complete threat
model. For Java Maven dependency facts, use the separate `module-boundary` and
`used-undeclared` rules with their documented project prerequisites.

Go imports are represented once per import spec, including grouped imports.
Patterns see `import ` followed by the optional alias and quoted package path;
diagnostic ranges identify the individual spec. Existing grouped imports do
not become new findings merely because another entry is added to the group.

After the user authorizes a policy change and supplies the intended boundary,
the candidate configuration can contain:

```yaml
rules:
  import-boundary:
    enabled: true
    required: true
    severity: error
    parameters:
      forbidden_imports:
        rust: ['^use crate::interfaces::internal']
        typescript: ['^import .* from legacy-internal/']
```

The mapping permits supported language names or `all`; each value is a bounded
array of valid regular expressions. Enabling `import-boundary` without this
mapping is a configuration error rather than an empty successful check.

## Agent workflow

1. Read the relevant file under `references/rules/` and this guide.
2. Run `rules list --format json` using the selected bundled executable.
3. Explain the rule's snapshot evidence, default severity, and limits.
4. Confirm that the task covers the candidate-policy change; use existing
   authorization and ask only for a missing material choice or required approval.
   Do not invent a severity or architecture boundary.
5. Follow [repository verification](verification.md) and report warnings,
   violations, and incomplete evidence separately.

The optional `lang-java` package adds twelve fixed-Java source-pattern reviews for direct concurrency, resource, locale, exception and security signals. See the repository Java rule triage guide for exact scope; comments, strings, aliases and multiline forms limit lexical findings.

## Historical review signals

These three rules require explicit selection and default to `required: false`,
`severity: warning`. Each inspects added lines of supported source files only.

| Rule | Scope | Default signal |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cpp-disabled-test` | C++ | `DISABLED_` marker; review reason, tracking issue and replacement coverage |
| `c-ignored-atomic-cas` | C and C++ | `(void)` discard of `atomic_compare_exchange_weak/strong`, including `_explicit`; review failure handling |
| `workaround-marker` | Supported source languages | `workaround`, `temporary fix`, `暂时规避`, `临时方案`, `临时绕过`; review root-cause issue, owner/expiry and removal plan |

Matches are review signals, not proof of semantic defects or missing metadata.
Adding a reason, issue or replacement-test reference does not suppress a marker.
Restoring the test, handling the result or removing the temporary implementation
can remove its signal; deleting explanatory comments alone does not prove repair.
Comments/literals can match, multiline/indirect calls can escape detection, and
`.h` is classified as C (outside `cpp-disabled-test`). Markdown is not scanned.

Use the [review cards](review-pack.md) for contextual review and
[design review](design-review.md) for Clean Code, Clean Architecture, DRY and SOLID
tradeoffs. Literal diagnostic message/fix metadata belongs to the built-in YAML;
it provides guidance without proving the concern or changing the verdict.
Existing parameter configuration can select an ecosystem-specific CAS API; this override replaces
the default patterns, so retain standard patterns explicitly if both are needed:

```yaml
schema_version: 1
rulesets: [lang-c]
rules:
  c-ignored-atomic-cas:
    enabled: true
    required: false
    severity: warning
    parameters:
      prohibited_patterns:
        c: ['\(\s*void\s*\)\s*ngx_atomic_cmp_set\s*\(']
        cpp: ['\(\s*void\s*\)\s*ngx_atomic_cmp_set\s*\(']
```

This configured symbol does not imply cross-language or general CAS coverage.
C++ gtest test-entity extraction and naming remain deferred; a name regex can
express `_when_`, but cannot supply the missing entity producer.

# Progressive discovery and candidate configuration

Built-in discovery works without a repository configuration and does not change
rule selection. Use the selected `--root` and `--config` consistently:

```bash
qualitygate rules categories --format json
qualitygate rules list --category test --language rust --source builtin --format json
qualitygate rules describe test-naming --format json
```

Reading a frozen policy context also requires a Git reference containing the
selected configuration; an absent configuration at `HEAD` is an error:

```bash
qualitygate rules context --category test --policy-ref <selected-ref> --format json
```

[Repository verification](verification.md) owns the missing-configuration and
initialization workflow. Discovery does not bypass that prerequisite for checks.

For a candidate-policy change covered by the task's existing authorization, use
validated CLI mutations:

```bash
qualitygate rules categories create migration --description "API migration" --format json
qualitygate rules assign import-boundary --category migration --format json
qualitygate rules categories rename migration api-migration --format json
qualitygate rules configure import-boundary --param 'forbidden_imports.rust=["^crate::interfaces"]' --format json
qualitygate rules enable import-boundary --format json
qualitygate rules disable import-boundary --format json
qualitygate rules categories delete api-migration --force --format json
```

Use only the caller's actual import boundary. Categories are mutable labels;
assignment does not activate a rule. Starter names are core, test, security,
architecture, style and project. Rename preserves starter identity and moves
assignments atomically. Delete needs `--force` when explicit assignments remain;
forced removal removes only that category's memberships. Repeated assignments
add categories, and `rules unassign <id> --category <name>` removes one. Removing
the last explicit membership restores the origin default; if that origin was
deleted, the rule has no category until reassigned. Rule rows expose the full
`categories` array and a legacy first `category`.

Filtered reads always retain `mandatory` rules and `mandatory_checks` separately
from selected rows. Context uses this policy precedence:

- An active signed policy selects the immutable active package, including when
  `--policy-ref` is omitted. A supplied ref must match the active reference;
  historical replay belongs to candidate validation.
- Without an active policy, `--policy-ref <selected-ref>` reads the configuration
  and rules from that commit and reports `caller_supplied_ref` trust.
- Without either, context reads the local candidate with `local_candidate` trust.

Read the returned `policy_digest` and trust label. A caller-selected ref alone
is not independent approval. `rules categories list` is also accepted.

`rules describe` exposes parameter types, descriptions, defaults and schema
fragments; language descriptors also expose whether the effective parameter is
required. A fixed scope requires the declared list; a subset scope accepts only
a nonempty subset of declared languages. Omit an override to inherit its default,
rather than using an empty list to bypass scope. Schema string-length checks do
not replace UTF-8 byte budgets, Rust regex validation or other semantic checks.
`--param key=JSON` requires JSON values, including quoted strings. Dotted paths
retain sibling object values; an undotted object replaces the entire parameter.
Repeat `--param` for one atomic edit. `configure` also accepts `--severity` and
`--required true|false`; new configured rules start disabled. Project DSL
assertions are managed in rule definitions, not through parameters. Built-in
`diagnostic` message/fix metadata belongs to the shipped rule definition and
changes presentation only; it is not a configurable policy parameter or verdict.

All mutations require an existing candidate config and support `--config`.
They preserve unrelated settings and inherited defaults, validate before atomic
replacement, preserve file permissions and reject conflicting writers. A killed
writer leaves `<config>.lock`; verify that it has stopped before explicitly
recovering the lock. Retain mutation JSON (operation, changed flag, before/after
digests and result) with the command log and reviewed Git diff. Changed YAML is
normalized; semantic no-ops preserve original bytes.

Source reviews and policy trust remain separate. Executable changes can make
existing source-review bindings stale; check reports retain missing/stale
evidence. Neither a category operation nor configuration success approves a
policy or establishes a passing gate.

Discovery reads policy/rule directories without scanning repository sources.
Once an evidence/policy archive exists, semantic policy edits require an explicit
candidate ID. Use `policy candidate create` with the caller-selected parent,
actor, reason and retained evidence, followed by `policy candidate rules`.
After signed promotion, `rules context`, inventory and ordinary checks select
the immutable active package; category edits cannot weaken mandatory rules.

For an authorized policy evolution workflow, use externally supplied suite,
trust and approval files. External protected files and retained logs accept
native absolute paths on Windows and POSIX; they must remain outside the
checked repository, without traversal or symlink ancestors, within read limits.
Repository-relative rule paths still require forward slashes.
See [operations](operations.md) for snapshot materialization, external temporary
storage and execution budgets. Missing or changed inputs remain incomplete;
reducing the checked inventory is not a repair.
`policy candidate validate` compares pinned replay,
held-out and anchor tasks with bounded parallelism. `policy candidate
approval-subject` produces the exact signing subject, `approve` verifies the
independent human signature, and `promote` rechecks it before activation.
Never manufacture an approval or private key. Missing tools/evidence and
timeouts remain incomplete. `policy rollback-subject` and `policy rollback`
require a distinct external signature and preserve the historical transition.

`rules revalidate`, `demote`, `deprecate`, `retire` and `revoke` take
`--candidate`, `--actor` and `--reason`; they prepare candidate changes and do
not grant approval. `rules history` exposes evidence and lifecycle states.
`policy effectiveness` separates oracle validity, observed rule/check use and
runtime from unknown downstream benefit, context tokens and review effort.
Only results with matching suite, parent, evaluator epoch/digest, environment,
budget and job count share a longitudinal group.
Project rule reads and schema parsing use at most eight workers, with 256 files,
1 MiB content and 4,096 directory-entry limits. Catalog errors and timeouts remain
errors even when the selected category would otherwise be empty.

# Bundled built-in rule guide

The YAML files in `references/rules/` are the versioned built-in rule assets read by the
matching Qualitygate CLI at runtime. Read this guide and the relevant YAML
before proposing a rule. Then use `qualitygate rules list --format json` to
verify what the installed executable can enforce. Do not edit the Skill assets
to change a repository policy; a repository policy selects and configures
rules, while the executable owns evaluation.

## Selection boundary

Use `rules list --language java --source builtin --format json` for built-ins,
`--source project` for `qualitygate/rules` (or an explicit legacy policy path),
and `--source all` for both. An empty definition language scope adds no language
filter; each implementation still determines supported files and capabilities.
Built-in inventory queries need no initialized policy and include all shipped
packages, even unselected ones; listing does not enable enforcement. When IDs
overlap, both origins remain visible and only the selected one can be enabled.

Listing a rule is read-only. Adding or enabling rules changes candidate policy
and must be covered by the task's authorization; do not ask again when it is
already provided. Ordinary initialization follows the automatic missing-config
prerequisite in [repository verification](verification.md); it does not authorize
`--with-checks`, rule enabling, or policy adoption. A rule's archived
`standard_refs` and `lifecycle_inputs` are provenance for the packaged
definition, not an implicit mandate for every repository.

Prefer the smallest rule set that matches the user's request. A warning can
produce diagnostics while leaving the overall gate non-blocking; it still
needs a reported disposition. Missing syntax, policy, snapshot, or required
execution evidence is incomplete validation, never a clean result.

## General language rules

| Rule | Languages | Default | Use it for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `test-naming` | Java, Python, Rust, TypeScript, Go | error | added test discovery names |
| `test-naming-strict` | Java | error | added test names matching a team pattern |
| `test-annotation-dependency` | Java | error | annotated added tests and resolved Maven dependency facts |
| `no-hardcoded-secrets` | Java | error | literal credential patterns in added files |
| `no-printf-log` | C, C++ | error | `printf` or `fprintf` call patterns in added native files |
| `no-unsafe-string` | C, C++ | error | `strcpy`, `sprintf`, `strcat`, or `gets` call patterns in added native files |
| `no-test-sleep` | all languages | error | `sleep`, `usleep`, or `nanosleep` call patterns in added test paths |
| `no-bare-except` | Python | error | bare exception handler patterns in added files |
| `no-os-path` | Python | error | selected `os.path` calls in added files |
| `no-print` | Python | warning | `print` calls in added files |
| `no-emoji` | all languages | error | configured emoji Unicode ranges in added UTF-8 files |
| `python-test-naming` | Python | error | lower snake case added pytest test names |
| `parameterized-tests` | Java, Python, Rust, TypeScript, Go | warning | repeated added test shapes |
| `comment-language` | supported parsed comments | warning | an explicitly selected comment-language convention |
| `security-sensitive-api` | Java, Python, Rust, TypeScript, Go | warning | changed uses of configured high-risk API patterns |
| `todo-marker` | supported source files | warning | changed `TODO`, `FIXME`, or `XXX` work markers |

`security-sensitive-api` uses bounded, single-line regex patterns on changed
source lines: Java process launch APIs, Python `eval`/`exec` and pickle loads,
Rust `unsafe` blocks, TypeScript dynamic evaluation/process execution, and Go
process execution. A match is a review signal, not proof of an exploitable
path. Override `parameters.prohibited_patterns` only with reviewed,
language-keyed regex arrays. `paths` can narrow files; `languages` must remain a
nonempty subset of the declared languages. An omitted override inherits the
scope; `languages: []` is rejected. Consult `rules describe security-sensitive-api`
for the runtime parameter contract before editing.

`todo-marker` uses the same bounded changed-line engine. It asks for an
explicit decision about deferred work rather than assuming that every marker is
a defect or should be deleted.

`commit-message-convention` is a core rule with a ticket-prefixed default
subject pattern. Configure `parameters.pattern` for the team's convention.
`test-naming-strict` defaults to `^should_.+_when_.+` on added Java tests.
`test-annotation-dependency` defaults to `@Test` and
`org.junit.jupiter:junit-jupiter-api`; set `annotation`, `group`, and
`artifact` to the actual project contract, and provide a snapshot-bound Maven
facts producer through `depends_on`. Missing facts are incomplete validation
when an annotated added test is selected; an empty selection passes without a
configured producer prerequisite. Configured prerequisites still run.
`no-hardcoded-secrets` checks added Java files with a configurable single-line
regex and does not prove that every secret or live credential was found.
These Java rules are opt-in and keep a fixed Java scope.

The three Issue 10 rules are also opt-in. `no-printf-log` and
`no-unsafe-string` inspect added C/C++ files with a fixed `languages: [c, cpp]`
scope, including `.h` headers. `no-test-sleep` uses an empty language scope
and defaults to common test directory and filename globs; configure `paths`
for a repository's test layout. All three scan UTF-8 file lines with bounded
regular expressions. Matches in comments and strings can be false positives;
they do not establish a parsed call or prove that a replacement API is safe.
Files outside the selected paths, modified files, and nonmatching languages
are not inspected. Unreadable selected bytes or exhausted analysis budgets
make the check incomplete.
